newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P assigns Bnk of Asia counterparty rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns Bnk of Asia counterparty rating.

text.p: Standard and Poor's said on Monday it had assigned its "BB plus" long- and "B" short-term counterparty credit ratings to Bank of Asia Public Co Ltd.
A stable outlook was also assigned to the bank, it said.
The ratings reflected the bank's strong profitability and sound capital ratios, it said.

Compared with other Thai banks, Bank of Asia's profile was characterised by a weaker market position, a higher level of non-performing assets and a greater reliance on foreign currency funding, S&P said.
Bank of Asia is one of the smaller domestic Thai banks with a market share of bank assets of about 2.42 percent at year-end 1995.

S&P said in an increasing competitve Thai banking environment, Bank of Asia did not have a leadership position in any of the business areas in which it operated and directly competed with the larger Thai banks for market share.
The bank is currently undertaking an extensive review of its distribution network and technology platforms to make it more competitive in the retail market.

The rating outlook is stable, reflecting S&P's view that the bank's asset quality and funding profile should strengthen as non-performing loans continue to decline and as the benefits of its retail strategy were realised, it said.
